title: QUICK PRO ER:ONE - China's Latest Aero Bike

takeaways.text: Tire clearance is limited to 32 mm, mainly at the chainstays, because the team uses 56T chainrings; T47 (68 mm) bottom bracket.
The presenter's size-small aero build (65/75 mm wheels, wireless semi-wired groupset, 54/38 rings) weighed 7.415 kg with pedals, cages and mount.

Feels like a battering ram: slower to change direction and accelerate than the lighter AR:ONE but very fast once up to speed; most of the presenter's sponsored team preferred it, while a climber preferred the AR:ONE.
Dislikes: the front brake hose exits the aero fork high up, no lower bottle-cage position for single-bottle use, and weight for a weight-focused buyer.

A size-small frame in the lightest gloss paint weighed 910 g with both derailleur hangers; the presenter's repeatedly resprayed prototype was about 1,070–1,080 g. Quick Pro's figure is 840 g unpainted for a medium.
In June 2025 the frameset was US$1,999 or US$2,099 depending on paint at the presenter's store, US$100 more than the AR:ONE.

disclosure: China Cycling's founder also leads Panda Podium, and the video links to that retailer's ER:ONE listing.
summary: Model-specific walkaround and ride discussion for the ER:ONE; exact current China SKU, price, specification, and warranty remain publication blockers.
